left.tested_scope: Crash-consistent OUTER evaluation state machine with durable intents, stable per-cell logical IDs, reconcile-before-execute, immutable outcomes, deterministic certification, and six real SIGKILL recovery boundaries in a SQLite-backed provider simulator.

right.tested_scope: LongMemEval-derived memory-poisoning study of simple false-assertion poisoning, write-time content screening, and additive provenance weighting. Plainly worded false assertions equal to 1.2% of the corpus reduced accuracy from 0.850 to 0.300; a screening pipeline with 0.832 indirect-prompt-injection recall rejected 0 of 360 poisoned memories; shipped provenance weighting was statistically indistinguishable from no defense (p=0.80); stronger trust weighting improved poisoned-corpus accuracy to 0.7000 when untrusted content was mostly benign, but when answer-bearing evidence itself came through the untrusted channel, evidence recall fell to zero and accuracy to 0.0417. The claimed no-usable-setting result is bounded to the measured similarity regime and additive weighting formulation.

comparison.semantic_overlap: Only a very broad reliability theme overlaps: both expose failure when a system relies on a coarse proxy instead of preserving the state needed for the actual correctness obligation. terminal_outer_sigkill_reference addresses execution-effect identity and recovery after process death; FE-359 addresses memory integrity versus availability when content screening or scalar provenance trust is used under adversarial retrieval. They do not share a tested mechanism, failure boundary, state representation, intervention, or evaluation endpoint.
distinguishing_scope: terminal_outer_sigkill_reference tests crash consistency, duplicate-effect avoidance, durable intent/outcome reconciliation and deterministic certification across six real SIGKILL boundaries; it does not test memory poisoning, retrieval similarity, provenance weighting, untrusted evidence recall or screening defenses.

FE-359 tests poisoning resistance and denial of legitimate untrusted evidence under content screening and additive provenance weighting in LongMemEval-derived corpora; it does not test process-death recovery, stable logical effect IDs, reconcile-before-execute, durable effect intents or SIGKILL resilience.

phase1_hard_gates.reason: This is pairwise deduplication evidence only. The left tested scope relies on local subprocess/SIGKILL execution plus a SQLite-backed provider simulator. FE-359 is a bounded memory-defense failure study, not a complete scheduled-Chat-native dependency-elimination route. The pair therefore establishes no accepted end-to-end Phase-1 route.
